title: Sidewalk snow clearing and three development proposals
subtitle: Community Services business plan, Order of Canada recognition, accessibility committee appointments and informal public meetings on three planning applications.
overview: Council's first meeting of 2023 made few formal decisions. Most of the evening was spent on presentations and informal public meetings, where no decisions are made. Council heard the Community Services business plan, including recreation, parks, fire and enforcement priorities ahead of budget deliberations, and two resident delegations asking the city to take over sidewalk snow clearing. Staff said a winter control discussion paper is coming and that nothing is currently in the budget for expanding city clearing.

Council approved appointments to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee for a four-year term, pending ratification by the partnering municipalities {{vote:m4}}. It also agreed to attend an all-Council training session on January 27 {{vote:m5}}. Council recognized two Order of Canada recipients from Waterloo.

Three planning applications were presented at informal public meetings: a three-tower mixed-use proposal at Bridgeport Road East and Weber Street North, a six-storey apartment building in Northdale, and a townhouse development on Erbsville Road. Staff will report back at later formal public meetings, where residents can comment again. Council also held a closed meeting at the start of the session on labour relations and committee appointments; the minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved report CAO2023-009 and appointed eight applicants, including one agency representative, to a four-year term ending December 31, 2026, pending ratification by the partnering municipalities {{vote:m4}}.
Council agreed to attend an all-Council training meeting on Friday, January 27, 2023, from 9:00 a.m. to noon {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Two resident delegates argued that relying on property owners to clear sidewalks within 24 hours is inequitable and ineffective. They said it affects seniors, people with disabilities and people without cars, and asked for funding for a pilot, possibly starting with busy sidewalks near high-rises, transit and shops.

One delegate cited a staff discussion paper showing complaints about uncleared sidewalks more than tripled between 2020 and 2022 even as enforcement increased. They said this shows the enforcement approach is not working.

Councillors raised concerns about doing sidewalk clearing properly. They cited slow service in other cities, the need to set clear expectations on timing and service levels, and the greenhouse gas impact of more equipment. Others suggested prioritizing routes near schools.

On the Bridgeport and Weber proposal, councillors asked about wind, shadow, traffic, electrical reliability, above-ground parking, rental housing and community benefits. The applicant said underground parking was not possible because of site contamination. It also said the traffic study showed acceptable service levels.

On the Erbsville Road townhouses, a delegate supported development in principle but raised concerns about the creek, wildlife corridor, floodplain, tree removal, small buffers, and the lack of sidewalks and trails. A councillor also asked about trail links, a sidewalk on Erbsville Road and stormwater planning.
